core.text: One stipulated 300 rpm trial stopped at second 60 and met the final-vial proxy at approximately 2.4 percent spread. Sustained 900 rpm and optical stability therefore lack universal necessity for this bounded exercise. Neither syringe success nor the proposed optical return loop has been observed.

Migration hypothesis: carry bulk redistribution with the needle-free syringe instead of rotation. With the stirrer off throughout, precommit six 20 mL low-position withdrawals and upper-side returns, one completed at each ten-second mark through second 60. Stop transfers regardless of images. Prediction: this fresh recipe meets the second-120 final-vial spread target of at most 4 percent, demonstrating a possible alternative carrier only if observed.

Second attack: remove the migrated carrier by performing zero redistribution transfers and zero stirring before the identical depth-sampling procedure. Prediction under syringe-dependent redistribution: final-vial spread exceeds 4 percent despite success of the migration arm. Prediction under passive redistribution or sampling-mediated apparent uniformity: both arms meet the target. This attack is distinct from replacing rotation with syringe transfer.

Use six fresh trials as two triplets: fixed 300 rpm for 60 seconds, syringe migration, and zero-transfer second attack. Reverse arm order in the second triplet; fix dye-addition location, bottle and camera per block. All active mixing ends at second 60, giving equal quiet intervals before second-120 sampling. Alternate sampling order, use common references, log images without operational feedback, report raw vial readings, transfers, stirring duration and failures, and retain spill-stop constraints.

residue.text: Only the original lower-speed sample success is established. Migration success followed by attack failure would support syringe-carried redistribution under this recipe, without proving unique necessity. Migration failure would leave the proposed transfer dose unresolved. Success in both arms would weaken the syringe-dependency claim but would not distinguish passive transport from sampling disturbance. Specks remain unidentified; repeatability is not calibration; absolute concentration, bubbles and external generalization remain unestablished.

tension.account_a: Hypothesis: six low-to-high syringe transfers supply redistribution required to meet the bounded depth-vial target when rotation is absent.
tension.account_b: Incompatible hypothesis for this comparison: the target is achieved without those transfers through passive redistribution or sampling-mediated equalization.
tension.prediction_a: Migration arm passes, but the zero-transfer second attack fails; replicated separation supports account A within the stipulated recipe.
tension.prediction_b: Migration and zero-transfer second-attack arms both pass; success survives removal of the new carrier, favoring account B over account A.
